findings.statement: _entry_rows resolves a reviewed sidecar pin independently for every package entry; that helper reparses and fully validates the same YAML policy on every call.
evidence: scripts/build_external_audit_package.py:983-1026 loops over 555 entries and calls reviewed_active_binary_sidecar_pin at line 1013.
htt/src/common/cf4_p0_quarantine.py:2297-2318 shows that every helper call invokes load_policy at line 2314.
htt/src/common/cf4_p0_quarantine.py:547-560 reads and yaml.safe_load parses the policy; the remainder of load_policy validates paths, pins, sidecars, and artifact digests.
cProfile: build_audit_package_payload 88.806 s; _entry_rows 58.345 s; 559 load_policy calls 57.002 s; 564 yaml.safe_load calls 41.037 s.
Unprofiled baseline payload: 41.412723 s for 555 entries and 3268 scanned paths.
Process-local simulation of one validated policy snapshot for one build: 17.283692 s, with 559 call sites but one actual load; absolute saving 24.129031 s and relative saving 58.27%.
A second simulation covering payload plus build_zip_bytes took 33.614993 s: payload 17.563609 s and ZIP 16.051384 s, with 563 policy call sites and one actual load.
assumptions: The working tree remained unchanged during each isolated measurement.
The in-memory monkeypatch changed only repeated load_policy evaluation; it did not bypass source-byte, sidecar, Git HEAD, quarantine, or ZIP revalidation paths.
cProfile cumulative times have instrumentation overhead, so unprofiled timings are used for expected wall-time benefit.

findings.statement: Every payload performs an exhaustive repository quarantine validation, every ZIP build performs another, and the test module repeats both operations many times.
evidence: scripts/build_external_audit_package.py:1436-1476 revalidates all packaged bytes and calls assert_repository_clean once per ZIP build.
htt/src/common/cf4_p0_quarantine.py:2357-2453 enumerates and scans active repository paths; _repository_candidate_paths uses git ls-files at lines 1072-1099.
cProfile: validate_repository 24.631 s and _scan_text 6.211 s for one profiled payload.

Static call counting in tests/contracts/test_audit_package_generator.py finds 13 successful full payload constructions and 7 ZIP constructions: six _payload calls, one direct payload call, six CLI payloads, four direct/fixtureless ZIP builds, and three CLI ZIP builds. This implies 20 exhaustive validation passes in this test module.
The exact source-only --check observation supplied by the main writer was 41.99 s at 103% CPU and 183564 KiB RSS before reporting a stale manifest.
assumptions: The static count describes the successful paths in the current tests; early-failing negative payload tests were excluded because they do not reach repository validation.

findings.statement: Per-binary Git binding launches many subprocesses, but it is not the cause of the order-of-magnitude delay.
evidence: htt/src/common/package_binary_binding.py:133-166 invokes git rev-parse and git show for same-path HEAD byte checks; verify_package_binary_binding invokes this path at lines 402-449.
cProfile: 825 verify_package_binary_binding calls consumed 3.372 s; 1009 subprocess.run calls consumed 2.510 s; _repository_candidate_paths itself consumed 0.259 s.
assumptions: Git object data was warm enough for the measured run; cold storage could increase this component, but it remains below repeated YAML validation in the measured profile.
